name: Court piece
summary: Four-player fixed-partnership trick-taking game where one player declares trump after seeing five cards and first to seven tricks wins.
rules_text: Played by four players in two fixed partnerships with a 52-card deck, counter-clockwise. Dealer is random. Five cards are dealt to each player in batches. The player after dealer, the trump-caller, looks at their five cards and announces trump suit. Others only then look. Remaining cards are dealt. Trump-caller leads first trick. Players must follow suit if possible; otherwise may play any card including trump. The highest trump wins, otherwise the highest card of led suit wins. Winner leads next. Play normally stops when one side has won seven tricks. Winning the first seven tricks is a kot/kap, winning all 13 is a bavney/baunie bonus. If trump-caller has no court cards in first five, or a player has none at all, a redeal may be called. No table talk is allowed.
rating_reason: Team trick-taking, trump selection, win seven tricks.
